name: Seeed XIAO ESP32C5
radio: the SoC's own radios: wifi24, wifi5, ble, ieee802154

flash.bootloader_instructions: Hold BOOT while plugging in USB; release after a second. The chip's USB-JTAG-serial port appears.
flash.note: Values from public documentation; not yet verified on a board of this kind (the target is experimental until then).

usb.when: ESP32-S3/C5 USB-JTAG-serial (download mode and, with CDC on boot, the running firmware)

pins.name: IO27
pins.note: yellow user LED (kitsune's DATA_PIN); IO27 in the DevKitC-1 CircuitPython build's pin names

led.note: one yellow LED on GPIO27 (kitsune: on for every state except red)

battery.divider_note: Powered from USB or a 5 V pack. kitsune's note: the pack must not have a low-current cut-off, or the board never wakes from deep sleep.

notes: The only kitsune board with 5 GHz Wi-Fi and an 802.15.4 radio (Zigbee coordinator). kitsune builds it with the pioarduino platform fork. kitsune notes client mode gets the wrong MAC on this board. Bootloader offset 0x2000 is the ESP32-C5 convention; to be confirmed with the first board.
Power: kitsune foxes sleep between transmissions; a USB power bank with a low-current auto-off cuts power during the sleep and the fox never wakes (kitsune's README). Use a pack without auto-off.
Serial: native USB — the console port disappears while the chip sleeps and returns when it wakes (kitsune's README: 'Serial console during sleep: no'). 'serial port dropped' each cycle is expected.

serial.notes: kitsune prints 'ESP32 boot count', 'Awake and screaming', 'Going to sleep' and 'PANIC' on its serial port; no command interface.

circuitpython.note: CircuitPython has no XIAO ESP32C5 build (checked 2026-10-24); the ESP32-C5-DevKitC-1-N8R8 build is the same chip and runs here, reporting espressif_esp32c5_devkitc_1_n8r8 — the same id the FireBeetle 2 ESP32-C5 reports, so the page keeps whichever of the two is selected. Pin names are the DevKit's IOxx. To verify on the board.
